text:
jun: hey all  first day! quick practical rule-check: where's the best place to post laptop/VPN/wifi hiccups vs who-owns/process questions vs a quick intro? also onboarding-bot is pinging me a lot, any neat ways to quiet it for a few days? :wave:

onboarding-bot: welcome Jun! A short cheat: hardware/connectivity -> DM @infra-oncall or post in #help if you want others to see. Process/who-owns -> #new-hires for cross-team answers, or the specific team channel (e.g., #eng or #product) for team-scoped questions. Intro -> #introductions (1-line: timezone, role, repos you need). To quiet me, DM me `snooze 3d` or `preferences digest` for once-daily rollups.

infra-oncall: if it's VPN/wifi send `/ticket create "VPN connect" --body "os, device, error"` or DM with `diag collect` output so we can triage. If it's hardware (battery, screen) specify serial number. Typical response: 1-4 hours.

amanda: couple of channel hygiene tips: 1) use threads for follow-ups so the main channel isn't flooded; 2) reactions for quick ack (:eyes:, :thumbsup:); 3) if it's a private matter (pay, schedule, health) DM the person or use #people-ops.

kevin: on access requests: check pinned messages in #dev-access first. We use an access repo flow for most cloud/repos: open a tiny PR listing who to add and why, tag the owner. If you need an expedited path, mention @kevin or @infra-oncall with the PR link.

jun: helpful! what's the good heuristic for DM vs thread?

amanda: DM for one-off private stuff or to escalate. Thread for anything that helps others or where discussion is likely. If you're unsure, post a one-line in #new-hires like "route: access -> who should I tag?" and people will point you.

infra-oncall: etiquette/security note: never paste full keys, tokens, or credentials. If you must share logs with secrets, redact or attach to a ticket. We have a vault integration recommended in pinned resources.

onboarding-bot: pro tip: if onboarding reminders are too chatty you can: `snooze 3d`, `snooze until 2026-05-01`, or `preferences quiet` to only get critical items. Also try `digest daily` to reduce noise.

jun: love the digest option. one last tiny Q: do people prefer multiple related small questions in one post or separate posts?

amanda: bundle related micro-questions into a single message so threads stay coherent. If they diverge into different topics, split into separate threads with a short subject line at the start like "access: infra repos".

kevin: final note: check channel topics and pinned items first; they usually contain the access flow, troubleshooting steps, and links to the onboarding checklist. If something is missing, post in #new-hires and tag @onboarding-bot to get a checklist update.

jun: thanks everyone! posting a 1-liner intro in #introductions now (UTC-8, infra eng, needs access to infra/*). snoozed the bot for 3 days. really appreciate the quick orientation :smile:
